To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Remittances have a significant impact on rural welfare, and that this effect is positive in both of the villages we study.

remittances from migrants in the US to Mexico and from migrants in Mexico to the US are both equalizing and favorable in terms of their impact upon income inequality and welfare in rural villages in Mexico.

(1) remittances have the potential to reduce rural inequality and poverty, and (2) the extent to which remittances reduce rural inequality and increase rural welfare depends on the distribution of remittance-enhancing characteristics across households.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of migrant income on income inequality and rural development in Mexico.
the impact of migrant income on the distribution of village income by size and the impact of this on rural welfare.
the impact of remittances upon the distribution of rural incomes and rural welfare.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
remittances from US migrants to Mexico have a positive and equalizing impact upon the distribution of rural incomes.
the impact of remittances upon the distribution of income in rural villages is a complex function of the distribution of human capital and the migration opportunities available to village households.
remittances have a positive effect on income inequality in rural Mexico.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the impact of remittances upon the distribution of village incomes depends upon the degree to which remittances embody human capital and whether migration opportunities are diffused through a village population.
the impact of migrant income on inequality is not a simple one.
migration is a powerful tool to reduce poverty and inequality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
migration and remittances are not necessarily a one way street from the poor to the rich.
remittances have a positive effect on rural welfare in both villages. However the effects are larger and
the effect of migration on rural welfare is a complicated and context-dependent process.
